text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumping(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Michael ::: the person Michael.
Windy ::: the person Windy.
Peter ::: the person Peter.
EveryoneElse(y) ::: y is any person other than Michael.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) ∀ y ≠ Michael ::: Michael is taller than everyone else.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: Transitivity of taller relation.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
¬CanBlock(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jumping(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Anyone who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.

Conclusion:
¬CanBlock(Peter, Windy) ::: Peter cannot block Windy's shooting.
